body:
The error message is not fine.  The error message says you're importing `BrowserAnimationsModule` incorrectly.  This put me on track to trying to figure out how I was loading BrowserAnimationsModule incorrectly in my lazy loading modules after one of the few  breaking change in Angular 4.x.

The problem had nothing to do with importing BrowserAnimationsModule; I just forgot to include the animations property on my component.  Oops.  Now I'm here.
Thanks @johnchristopherjones ! Your comment made me realize I had the same issue. `BrowserAnimationsModule` was imported correctly, but I simply forgot to use `animations` in my component.

issue.title: Animation on host with trigger imported from file

repository.name: jest-preset-angular

body: Just had the same problem, but my issue was slightly different. I had the HostBinding in a component I moved animations out of during a refactor.
Thanks @johnchristopherjones! I spent an hour debugging this and I even reinstalled angular, but this solved it!

Lost a lot of time to this error message. Turns out when I tried to create the template variable `#sidenav` I had fat-fingered it to `@sidenav`, subsequently spending the next two hours trying to figure out why browser animations weren't being imported correctly, much less why they were involved at all.

Thanks @johnchristopherjones. The error message is totally misleading. I've waited an hour or two googling & staring at my package.json. 

How about something like "Hey you forgot to include an animation for @fooState."
